question: Indian socialism is a mixture of ________ (RPF Constable 2018 (05/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Capitalism and Gandhian
Communism and Socialism
Marxism and Gandhism
Communism and Gandhian
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Marxism and Gandhism

Explanation:
Indian socialism is a unique blend of Marxism and Gandhism. It rejects the extremes of capitalism and communism. From Marxism, it adopts the goal of economic equality and a classless society, while from Gandhism, it incorporates non-violence, sarvodaya (welfare of all), and decentralization. The term 'socialist' was added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment. Indian socialism does not abolish private property completely but emphasizes economic planning and social justice. This mixture suits India's diverse socio-economic conditions and aims to reduce inequality through peaceful means.

☛ Indian socialism is a mixture of which two ideologies? → Marxism and Gandhism
☛ Who propounded the term 'sarvodaya'? → Mahatma Gandhi

question: Which of the following is the head of the Indian Republic?  (RPF Constable 2018 (05/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Vice President
Chief Justice of India
Prime Minister
President
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is President

Explanation:
The head of the Indian Republic is the President. The Constitution of India declares the President as the first citizen of the country and the supreme commander of the armed forces. The President is elected by an electoral college consisting of elected members of both houses of Parliament and the legislative assemblies of the states. The term of office of the President is five years. While the Vice President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, the Prime Minister is the head of government, and the Chief Justice is the head of the judiciary.

question: The provision of judicial review in the Constitution of India was taken from _____ (RPF Constable 2018 (05/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Australian Constitution
French Constitution
Japanese Constitution
American Constitution
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is American Constitution

Explanation:
The provision of judicial review in the Constitution of India was taken from the American Constitution. Judicial review empowers the judiciary to examine the constitutionality of laws passed by the legislature or executive. In the US, this power was established in the landmark case of Marbury v. Madison (1803). In India, the Supreme Court and High Courts have the power of judicial review under Articles 13, 32, and 226. This system ensures the supremacy of the Constitution and protects fundamental rights. The judiciary also uses judicial review to safeguard the basic structure of the Constitution, as established in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973).

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ From which constitution is judicial review borrowed? → American
☛ Which case established judicial review in the US? → Marbury v. Madison (1803)
☛ Which articles in the Indian Constitution relate to judicial review? → Articles 13, 32, 226
☛ What is the scope of judicial review in India? → Subject to basic structure doctrine
☛ What is the purpose of judicial review? → To examine the constitutionality of laws
question_hi: भारत के संविधान में न्यायिक समीक्षा का प्रावधान ______ से लिया गया था (RPF Constable 2018 (05/02/2019) Shift 2)

फ़्रांसीसी संविधान
जापानी संविधान
अमेरिकी संविधान
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अमेरिकी संविधान

Explanation:
भारत के संविधान में न्यायिक समीक्षा का प्रावधान अमेरिकी संविधान से लिया गया है। न्यायिक समीक्षा का अर्थ है कि न्यायपालिका को विधायिका या कार्यपालिका द्वारा बनाए गए कानूनों की संवैधानिकता की जांच करने का अधिकार है। अमेरिकी संविधान में यह प्रावधान मार्बरी बनाम मैडिसन (1803) मामले में स्थापित हुआ था। भारत में, सर्वोच्च न्यायालय और उच्च न्यायालयों को संविधान के अनुच्छेद 13, 32 और 226 के तहत न्यायिक समीक्षा का अधिकार प्राप्त है। यह प्रणाली संविधान की सर्वोच्चता सुनिश्चित करती है और मौलिक अधिकारों की रक्षा करती है। न्यायिक समीक्षा के माध्यम से न्यायपालिका संविधान के मूल ढांचे की रक्षा करती है।

question: The Abolition of Untouchability comes under which fundamental right of Indian constitution? (RPF Constable 2018 (06/02/2019))
options: Right against Exploitation
Right to life
Right to Equality
Right to freedom of religion
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Right to Equality

Explanation:
The abolition of untouchability is enshrined in Article 17 of the Indian Constitution. This article falls under the Right to Equality (Articles 14-18). Untouchability is abolished, and its practice in any form is a legal offense. This provision was designed to ensure social equality and eliminate discrimination. Thus, the fundamental right it belongs to is the Right to Equality, not the Right against Exploitation, Right to Life, or Right to Freedom of Religion.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Under which part does Article 17 come? → Part 3 (Fundamental Rights)
☛ Which articles cover Right to Equality? → Articles 14-18
☛ Which article is responsible for social equality? → Article 15 and 17
☛ What is the practice of untouchability in India? → A legal offense

question: Who was called as the "Father of Local Self Government" in India? (RPF Constable 2018 (06/02/2019))
options: Lord Lytton
Lord Wellesley
Lord Ripon
Lord Curzon
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lord Ripon

Explanation:
Lord Ripon, who served as Viceroy of India from 1880 to 1884, is known as the Father of Local Self Government in India. In 1882, he passed a historic resolution, known as the Ripon Resolution, which laid the foundation for local self-government in India. This resolution introduced elected representation in local bodies, both rural and urban, and empowered them with democratic functions. Lord Ripon's efforts aimed at training Indians in democratic processes and administration, making him a pioneer of local governance. His reforms significantly contributed to the development of municipal administration in India.

question: The term socialist in the Preamble was added in which amendment of the Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2018 (06/02/2019))
options: 42nd amendment
10th amendment
44th amendment
24th amendment
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 42nd amendment

Explanation:
The term 'socialist' was added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, also known as the 'Mini Constitution'. This amendment, passed during the Emergency under Indira Gandhi's government, also added the words 'secular' and 'integrity' to the Preamble. It changed the description of India from 'sovereign democratic republic' to 'sovereign socialist secular democratic republic'. The 42nd Amendment brought several other significant changes, including the addition of Fundamental Duties and alterations to the powers of the judiciary. It remains one of the most controversial amendments in Indian constitutional history.

☛ Which amendment added 'integrity' to the Preamble? → 42nd Amendment (1976)

question: The traditional glove puppet show Pavakoothu belongs to _______ (RPF Constable 2018 (06/02/2019))
options: Andhra Pradesh
Karnataka
Kerala
Tamil Nadu
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Kerala

Explanation:
Pavakoothu is a traditional glove puppet show from Kerala, India. It is mainly practiced in the Palakkad district of Kerala. The puppets are made of wood and cloth and are worn on the hand like gloves. Performances depict mythological stories, especially from the Ramayana and Mahabharata. This art form is an important part of Kerala's rich folk tradition.

Explanation:
The Preamble of the Indian Constitution begins with 'We, the People of India', signifying that the authority of the Constitution is derived from the citizens of India. This reflects the fundamental spirit of democracy where sovereignty lies with the people. question: What type of Justice is guaranteed in the preamble of the Constitution of India? (RPF Constable 2018 (06/02/2019))
options: Social, Economic and Political Justice
Liberty
Equality
Fraternity
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Social, Economic and Political Justice

Explanation:
The Preamble of the Indian Constitution guarantees Social, Economic and Political Justice. These three dimensions of justice aim to provide fairness to every section of society. Social justice implies equal social opportunities and respect for all individuals. Economic justice means equitable distribution of economic resources and no economic exploitation. Political justice ensures equal participation in the political process, such as the right to vote and contest elections. Together, these three forms of justice lay the foundation for a just society and form one of the core objectives of the Constitution. By including them in the Preamble, the framers ensured that all state actions are based on these principles of justice. This tripartite classification of justice reflects the comprehensive vision of the Constitution to achieve a balanced and fair society.

question: What is the duration of Panchayats? (RPF Constable 2018 (06/02/2019))
options: 2 years
5 years
3 years
6 years
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 5 years

Explanation:
According to Article 243E of the Indian Constitution, every Panchayat has a tenure of 5 years from the date of its first meeting. If a Panchayat is dissolved before the completion of its term, fresh elections must be held within 6 months. This provision was introduced by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, which gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions. The term of the Panchayat is counted from the first meeting after its formation. In case of premature dissolution, the new Panchayat will serve only for the remaining period. The state government frames rules regarding the conduct of elections and tenure of Panchayats.

question: Which term was replaced instead of "Unity of the Nation" in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2018 (06/02/2019))
options: Harmony of the Nation
Equality of the Nation
Fraternity of the Nation
Unity and Integrity of the Nation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Unity and Integrity of the Nation

Explanation:
In the original Preamble of the Indian Constitution, the phrase 'Unity of the Nation' was used. The 42nd Amendment (1976) replaced it with 'Unity and Integrity of the Nation' to emphasize both national unity and territorial integrity. This amendment, enacted during the Emergency, also added the words 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' to the Preamble. The change aimed to strengthen the country's sovereignty and territorial cohesion. The Supreme Court in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) had earlier upheld the Preamble as part of the Constitution but amendable. The inclusion of 'Integrity' highlights the indivisibility of the nation against separatist tendencies.

question: An ordinance passed by the President ceases to operate _______ from the reassembly of Parliament. (RPF Constable 2018 (06/02/2019))
options: on the expiry of six months
by end of the session
on starting week
on the expiry of six weeks
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is on the expiry of six weeks

Explanation:
Under Article 123 of the Indian Constitution, the President has the power to promulgate ordinances when Parliament is not in session. An ordinance ceases to operate at the expiry of six weeks from the reassembly of Parliament, unless it is approved by both Houses. This provision ensures the supremacy of the legislature over the executive. If Parliament approves the ordinance, it becomes an act; otherwise, it lapses automatically. This is a constitutional safeguard to prevent misuse of legislative power by the executive. The ordinance must be laid before both Houses when Parliament reconvenes.

question: The Lok Adalat is based on (RPF Constable 2018 (06/02/2019))

Marxism

Explanation:
The Lok Adalat is based on Gandhian principles, especially non-violence and truth-force. It emphasizes amicable resolution of disputes. Lok Adalat is an alternative dispute resolution mechanism where cases are settled by mutual consent of the parties. This system is rooted in principles of conciliation, compromise, and justice. In Gandhian philosophy, justice is not merely a legal process but a tool for social harmony. Lok Adalats embody this philosophy, where judges and parties work together to find solutions. The system reduces court burden and promotes speedy justice.

question: When did the 86th Constitution Amendment Act come into force? (RPF Constable 2018 (08/02/2019))
options: 2009
2011
2010
2002
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 2002

Explanation:
The 86th Constitution Amendment Act, related to the Right to Education, came into force in the year 2002. This amendment inserted Article 21A in the Constitution, making education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14 years. It also modified Article 45 under the Directive Principles of State Policy to emphasize early childhood education. This amendment was a significant step toward ensuring free and compulsory education. Subsequently, the Right to Education Act (RTE) was enacted in 2009 and came into effect on 1 April 2010.

question: How many types of urban local government are there in India? (RPF Constable 2018 (08/02/2019))

Explanation:
There are eight types of urban local government in India: Municipal Corporation, Municipality, Nagar Panchayat, Notified Area Committee, Industrial Town Committee, Cantonment Board, Township, and Port Trust. The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act (1992) gave constitutional status to urban local bodies. Municipal Corporations are for large cities, Municipalities for smaller towns, and Nagar Panchayats for transitional areas. Other types are created for special needs like industrial areas, military zones, and ports. These bodies provide civic amenities such as water supply, roads, sanitation, and public health. They are elected by local residents and play a key role in decentralized urban governance.

question: What is the arrangement of local self-governing governments in rural areas? (RPF Constable 2018 (08/02/2019))

The main objective of Panchayati Raj is decentralized planning, rural development, and delivery of basic services. ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में स्थानीय स्वशासन की व्यवस्था को पंचायती राज कहा जाता है। यह भारतीय संविधान के भाग 9 में वर्णित त्रिस्तरीय ढांचे पर आधारित है, जिसमें ग्राम पंचायत, क्षेत्र पंचायत (ब्लॉक स्तर) और जिला पंचायत शामिल हैं। 73वें संविधान संशोधन 1992 ने इसे संवैधानिक दर्जा दिया। पंचायती राज संस्थाओं का उद्देश्य ग्रामीण विकास, स्थानीय नियोजन, और बुनियादी सेवाओं का संचालन करना है। अन्य विकल्प: ग्राम न्यायालय न्यायिक व्यवस्था का हिस्सा है, नगर पालिका शहरी क्षेत्रों के लिए है, और जिला परिषद पंचायती राज का एक स्तर है, लेकिन पूरी व्यवस्था को पंचायती राज ही कहा जाता है।
